courses.title: Charts First: Market Structure Before Exposure
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Foundations of chart reading and market structure

courses.title: Flow After Structure: Where Flowseeker Fits
courses.description: Flowseeker shows every options trade as it prints. Read the chart first, then the Heatseeker™ map, and only then weigh the flow against both. A print tells you what traded — not who, and not why.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Reading the tape: prints, side, sweeps and open interest

courses.title: Dealer Positioning and Gamma Mechanics
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Foundations of chart reading and market structure

courses.title: Reading a Print: What Traded and Where It Filled
courses.description: Read a print correctly before you interpret it: the exact contract, the premium (not just the size), how far from spot and expiration it traded — and where it filled against the bid and ask. Those fields narrow what a trade could be. They never tell you who made it.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Reading the tape: prints, side, sweeps and open interest

courses.title: Node Hierarchy
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Foundations of chart reading and market structure

courses.title: Sweeps and Multi-Leg Trades: Seeing the Whole Trade
courses.description: Some prints are pieces of something bigger. A sweep is one order split across several exchanges — it shows urgency, not intent. A multi-leg trade is several contracts traded together — and one leg on its own can look like a completely different bet. Read the whole trade before you name it.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Reading the tape: prints, side, sweeps and open interest

courses.title: Gamma Regime Awareness and Day Forecasting
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 2 - Gamma awareness, pattern recognition, and execution

courses.title: Volume, Open Interest and What Changed
courses.description: Volume counts contracts traded today. Open interest counts contracts still open, as of the last clearing. Volume above open interest makes a contract worth a look — it doesn't prove new positions. The next day's open interest can support a read, but it never tells you who traded.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 1 - Reading the tape: prints, side, sweeps and open interest

courses.title: Heatseeker Pattern Recognition
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 2 - Gamma awareness, pattern recognition, and execution

courses.title: Scores and a Readable Feed: Sorting Without Fooling Yourself
courses.description: Flow Score (−100 to +100) says which way a print is classified; premium rank and Vol/OI say how unusual it is. Both sort your attention — neither is a probability. Filters decide which prints you see: build each tab around one question, change one filter at a time, and keep a broad tab. A filtered feed reads the way you filtered it; the summary bar above it is market-wide.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 2 - Using the tools: scores, filters, views and one contract

courses.title: Execution Models: Trading the Deflection
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 2 - Gamma awareness, pattern recognition, and execution

courses.title: The Tools and One Contract: The Right View, an Honest Answer
courses.description: Each Flowseeker view answers a different question in a different unit: the Live Feed lists prints, the Scanner summarises contracts, the Tracker follows what you saved, and the Dark Feed shows stock trades with no options side. When one contract matters, open Contract Drilldown with a question you can test — its views all come from the same trades — and finish with a hypothesis, a conflict, or "not enough evidence".
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 2 - Using the tools: scores, filters, views and one contract

courses.title: Rolling Floors and Ceilings
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Advanced interpretation of rolling structure and velocity

courses.title: Flow Meets the Map and the Trinity
courses.description: Read a print against the same ticker's map, at the same expiry, and place its strike among the nodes. Flow is one reason the map reshuffles — not the only one. Then read SPX, SPY and QQQ side by side: agreement raises confidence modestly (SPX and SPY track the same index), and divergence is a warning. Every read ends with what would weaken it.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Flow in context: the map, the Trinity, the chart and disagreements

courses.title: Air Pockets, Liquidity Vacuums, and Velocity Mode
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Advanced interpretation of rolling structure and velocity

courses.title: Flow on the Chart: Letting the Pane Support the Read
courses.description: Atlas can show flow in a pane under the price chart. The bars show premium — dollars — not contracts, with calls and puts kept separate. Filter the pane the way you filter a feed, and use it to ask "did premium show up at my level?" — not to find entries on its own.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Flow in context: the map, the Trinity, the chart and disagreements

courses.title: Node Lifecycle, Delivery, and Target Validity
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Advanced interpretation of rolling structure and velocity

courses.title: When Price and Flow Disagree: List the Explanations First
courses.description: Sometimes price goes one way and the flow points the other. Don't pick a winner. State the mismatch, list every explanation that fits it, then look for the evidence that tells them apart. Until something separates them, a disagreement is a reason to reduce size or wait — not a signal.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 3 - Flow in context: the map, the Trinity, the chart and disagreements

courses.title: Cross-Index Confluence
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 4 - Cross-index confluence and real-time integration

courses.title: Playbooks, Routine and Review: Making It a Practice
courses.description: A playbook is a form for a hypothesis — location, map, flow, target, weakens if, decision — with flow never the trigger. The reward must be at least three times the risk, size is a separate decision, and no trade is always valid. Run the same simple day, save enough to review each decision (including the ones you skipped), and judge decisions, not outcomes.
courses.categoryDescription: Tier 4 - Playbooks, routine and honest review
